finishStory.markedParagraph: [Rebekah] was not able to have [children], so Isaac [prayed] for her. God answered, and Rebekah became pregnant with [twins]. One night, the babies were [wrestling] in her belly. God told her the two boys would become two [nations]. The firstborn boy, [Esau], was red and hairy. His brother [Jacob] came out holding his heel. Esau grew up to be a [hunter], while Jacob liked staying near the tents. One day Esau was [hungry] and wanted Jacob’s [stew]. Jacob asked him to trade away his [birthright]. Foolishly, Esau agreed to this deal, showing he didn't care about his birthright.

storyOrder.text: Isaac prayed for Rebekah, and she became pregnant.
God told Rebekah the twins would become two nations.
Esau was born first, and Jacob held onto his heel.

Esau asked Jacob for stew, and Jacob demanded his birthright.
Esau sold his birthright for bread and lentil stew.
God repeated His promises to Isaac.

The original source question pool includes rhetorical, contextual, group-response questions. Only six adapted worksheet MC questions were prepared; verify the remaining narrative question bank is faithfully preserved.
